stories.headline: Chakkakomban operation not India-Pakistan war, says Keralam Forest Minister Shibu Baby John
stories.title: Chakkakomban operation not India-Pakistan war, says Keralam Forest Minister Shibu Baby John
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Thiruvananthapuram: Keralam Forest Minister Shibu Baby John on Saturday said the operation to tranquilise and radio-collar wild elephant Chakkakomban in Chinnakanal, Idukki district, was not an India-Pakistan war and that no undue pressure should be put on the officials involved or the animal.
The Forest Department had undertaken the operation to radio-collar Chakkakomban, which frequently strays into human habitations, posing a threat to people's lives.
However, the three-day effort did not succeed, following which the department temporarily suspended the operation and decided to resume it later.
John said there was no instruction to radio-collar the elephant on that particular day, and the operation was intended to be carried out in a manner that would not cause the animal stress.
The officials involved had been given the authority to make any decision necessary to ensure the mission's success, he said, adding that they decided to suspend it after three days of efforts.
The minister also urged people to understand the mental stress faced by the officials involved in the operation.

Those involved in the operation are people who work to protect elephants and forests, and they are trying to do what is possible within the available limitations to ensure the safety and lives of our people," he said.

The Forest Department, which has a responsibility akin to that of a guardian in protecting wildlife, was being forced to take difficult decisions that caused considerable emotional distress to its personnel, he said.
The minister said he had personally witnessed the mental pressure officials faced during Friday meetings with the Head of the Forest Department and the Chief Wildlife Warden.

At the same time, the safety of people living in the area could not be overlooked, he said, pointing out the potential consequences if an elephant crossed a populated area and encountered a child on the way to school.
"Setting aside our personal likes and dislikes, we are compelled to take decisions in such situations that we believe are in the larger interest of the people," he said.
The minister said the officials involved in the operation had handled the situation with considerable maturity.

stories.headline: Punjab: In election season, bitter rivals are pals again
stories.title: Punjab: In election season, bitter rivals are pals again
stories.summary: BJP old-timers fear being sidelined twice over, by the Akalis and by turncoats queuing for tickets
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In rural Punjab they say a quarrel between relatives lasts only until the next viah (wedding) in the family.

This Gurpurab, six years after Harsimrat Kaur Badal walked out of the Modi cabinet over the farm laws, Amit Shah and Sukhbir Badal joined hands at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, signalling the Akali Dal’s return to the NDA.
It is also said that in Punjab politics, the photo album is always kinder than memory.
Sharing the frame with Shah and Badal was Ravneet Bittu, who not long back had said the BJP could not carry the Akali burden of drugs and sacrilege.
The surprise was Shah’s generosity.
The Akalis, he said, would remain the bada bhai.
He said the farm laws, over which Akalis had walked out of the NDA, no longer mattered since they were repealed.

Sukhbir called it “not merely a political alliance, but an emotional one”, invoked his father’s bond with Vajpayee and Advani, and announced that Prime Minister Narendra Modi would come to Moga on 8 December for Parkash Singh Badal’s birth anniversary.
Both sides spoke of Hindu–Sikh brotherhood, drugs and jobs.
It was the old Punjab, Punjabi, Punjabiyat script of 1996, dusted off for a new season.
But read the fine print.
No seat-sharing formula was announced.

stories.headline: Sebi working on new exchange for pre-IPO shares, consultation paper out soon: Tuhin Kanta Pandey
stories.title: Sebi working on new exchange for pre-IPO shares, consultation paper out soon: Tuhin Kanta Pandey
stories.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is exploring setting up a separate trading exchange for pre-IPO shares. The market regulator is working on the proposal and plans to issue a consultation paper soon. Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the proposal is under consideration and that further details would be shared through the consultation process.Speaking at CNBC Awaaz's Market Mahakumbh event, Pandey said the idea was among the measures being examined amid the significant expansion of India's IPO market over the past three to four years. He said the regulator was considering a separate trading platform for pre-IPO shares, adding that work on the proposal was already underway.Responding to a question on whether investors could trade unlisted and pre-IPO shares on such a platform, Pandey clarified that Sebi's proposal would be limited to companies preparing to launch an IPO. The regulator does not intend to cover the entire unlisted market, which comprises lakhs of companies.Also Read | From attracting FIIs to starting Demat 2.0 accounts, Sebi chair Tuhin Kanta Pandey lists 4 prioritiesPandey also indicated that investor protection would be an important consideration while designing the proposed mechanism. He said the regulator would need to work out the framework, including safeguards for investors and additional disclosure requirements.On the scope of the proposed platform, including whether it would cover companies across market capitalisations or be restricted to a particular category, Pandey reiterated that the mechanism would be linked to the IPO process. He made it clear that Sebi would not extend the proposed arrangement to companies not connected to an upcoming IPO.The SEBI chief did not provide a specific timeline for the proposed platform but said the consultation paper would be issued soon, after which more details would become available.Sebi curbs on GMPThe development comes just days after Sebi cautioned investors against relying on grey market premium (GMP) figures, describing them as unofficial, unverified and unregulated. The regulator also clarified that investors cannot use SEBI or stock exchange grievance redressal mechanisms to resolve disputes arising from such transactions.In an advisory issued on November 23, Sebi noted that GMP figures for upcoming IPOs were being widely circulated through websites, digital platforms and newspapers. It also flagged instances of such figures being shared by certain SEBI-registered intermediaries and market participants.The regulator said these premiums are often presented as indicators of an IPO's expected listing price or potential returns, despite having no regulatory backing.Sebi to ease FII onboarding processSebi is also looking to reduce the time required for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to complete onboarding formalities from several months to as little as five business days. The move is part of a broader review of regulations governing IPOs, corporate bonds and market technology.Also Read | Sebi chairman says looking into Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal to protect minority shareholdersSpeaking at an ASSOCHAM conference in New Delhi on Friday, Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey outlined four key priorities for the regulator: simplifying regulations, deepening markets to support economic growth, facilitating access for global investors and expanding the use of technology while maintaining adequate safeguards.Pandey also said Sebi had proposed doing away with the Additional Disclosure Framework for FPIs, a move aimed at bringing India's regulatory framework closer to global standards.The proposed changes come against the backdrop of India's equity market valuation crossing Rs 500 trillion, equivalent to more than 130% of GDP. Companies raised around Rs 9 trillion through equity and debt markets in the first seven months of the financial year, including approximately Rs 1.45 trillion through 235 initial public offerings (IPOs), Pandey said.“Can it serve an economy twice its present size, finance a wider range of enterprises and remain fair, stable and trusted?” he asked, referring to the challenge facing the market.

opening: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is exploring setting up a separate trading exchange for pre-IPO shares.
The market regulator is working on the proposal and plans to issue a consultation paper soon.
body: Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the proposal is under consideration and that further details would be shared through the consultation process.
Speaking at CNBC Awaaz's Market Mahakumbh event, Pandey said the idea was among the measures being examined amid the significant expansion of India's IPO market over the past three to four years.
He said the regulator was considering a separate trading platform for pre-IPO shares, adding that work on the proposal was already underway.

Responding to a question on whether investors could trade unlisted and pre-IPO shares on such a platform, Pandey clarified that Sebi's proposal would be limited to companies preparing to launch an IPO.
The regulator does not intend to cover the entire unlisted market, which comprises lakhs of companies.
Pandey also indicated that investor protection would be an important consideration while designing the proposed mechanism.
He said the regulator would need to work out the framework, including safeguards for investors and additional disclosure requirements.

On the scope of the proposed platform, including whether it would cover companies across market capitalisations or be restricted to a particular category, Pandey reiterated that the mechanism would be linked to the IPO process.
He made it clear that Sebi would not extend the proposed arrangement to companies not connected to an upcoming IPO.
The SEBI chief did not provide a specific timeline for the proposed platform but said the consultation paper would be issued soon, after which more details would become available.
Sebi curbs on GMPThe development comes just days after Sebi cautioned investors against relying on grey market premium (GMP) figures, describing them as unofficial, unverified and unregulated.
The regulator also clarified that investors cannot use SEBI or stock exchange grievance redressal mechanisms to resolve disputes arising from such transactions.
In an advisory issued on November 23, Sebi noted that GMP figures for upcoming IPOs were being widely circulated through websites, digital platforms and newspapers.
It also flagged instances of such figures being shared by certain SEBI-registered intermediaries and market participants.
The regulator said these premiums are often presented as indicators of an IPO's expected listing price or potential returns, despite having no regulatory backing.

Sebi to ease FII onboarding processSebi is also looking to reduce the time required for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to complete onboarding formalities from several months to as little as five business days.
The move is part of a broader review of regulations governing IPOs, corporate bonds and market technology.

Speaking at an ASSOCHAM conference in New Delhi on Friday, Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey outlined four key priorities for the regulator: simplifying regulations, deepening markets to support economic growth, facilitating access for global investors and expanding the use of technology while maintaining adequate safeguards.
Pandey also said Sebi had proposed doing away with the Additional Disclosure Framework for FPIs, a move aimed at bringing India's regulatory framework closer to global standards.
The proposed changes come against the backdrop of India's equity market valuation crossing Rs 500 trillion, equivalent to more than 130% of GDP.

Companies raised around Rs 9 trillion through equity and debt markets in the first seven months of the financial year, including approximately Rs 1.45 trillion through 235 initial public offerings (IPOs), Pandey said.
“Can it serve an economy twice its present size, finance a wider range of enterprises and remain fair, stable and trusted?” he asked, referring to the challenge facing the market.

In an advisory issued on November 23, Sebi noted that GMP figures for upcoming IPOs were being widely circulated through websites, digital platforms and newspapers.
The proposed changes come against the backdrop of India's equity market valuation crossing Rs 500 trillion, equivalent to more than 130% of GDP.

stories.title: Karnataka to launch ‘Delhi Chalo’ protest if Centre fails to release drought relief: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar

He said the State had not received any financial assistance from the Union government for drought relief and that no announcement had been made on the matter.

“Even today, the Central government has not given a single rupee, nor has it announced anything,” he said, pointing out that Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara had furnished the necessary details at a special Cabinet meeting.

He had earlier participated in a meeting convened by the DMK in Chennai and said another meeting involving political parties was scheduled in Delhi.
The parties would discuss the implications of the proposed changes before deciding their position, he said.

stories.headline: Tata Sons vs Tata Trusts: Caveats filed in Bombay HC, Supreme Court ahead of crucial November 30 board meeting
stories.title: Tata Sons vs Tata Trusts: Caveats filed in Bombay HC, Supreme Court ahead of crucial November 30 board meeting
stories.summary: Tata Sons has filed caveats in the Bombay High Court and Supreme Court after Tata Trusts failed to secure interim relief. The November 30 board meeting will proceed, but its decisions remain subject to the final court order.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Under Section 148A of the Code of Civil Procedure, a caveat safeguards a party against an ex parte order being passed without giving it an opportunity to present its arguments.
On Friday, Justice Abhay Ahuja of the Bombay High Court declined to grant interim relief to Tata Trusts, which collectively holds a 66% stake in Tata Sons.
The court scheduled the next hearing for January 21, 2027.
While the decision allows Tata Sons to proceed with its scheduled November 30 board meeting, resolutions passed during the meeting will remain subject to the final outcome of the litigation.
Two constituent entities of Tata Trusts — Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and RD Tata Trust (RDTT) — approached the court on Thursday, challenging Chandrasekaran’s reappointment for a third term.
The trusts also sought restrictions on the upcoming board meeting, whose agenda includes a proposed listing of Tata Sons.

At the centre of the legal battle is Section 121 of Tata Sons’ Articles of Association (AoA), which governs additional voting requirements involving nominee directors of Tata Trusts and the chairman’s casting vote.
During the September 17 board meeting, Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts and a nominee director on the Tata Sons board, opposed Chandrasekaran’s reappointment.
Venu Srinivasan, the other nominee director, supported the proposal.
The split between the two nominee directors prompted acting chairman Harish Manwani to exercise his casting vote.
All other board members supported Chandrasekaran’s reappointment.
Tata Trusts has argued that a split between its nominee directors means the requisite affirmative majority has not been secured.

stories.headline: India's FY28 fiscal deficit projected to stay unchanged at 4.3% of GDP: Deutsche Bank
stories.title: India's FY28 fiscal deficit projected to stay unchanged at 4.3% of GDP: Deutsche Bank
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank warns FY28 consolidation faces rising pay, subsidies and oil-linked costs, even as cushions keep the deficit at 4.3% of GDP
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India's fiscal deficit for the financial year 2028 is projected to remain unchanged at 4.3 per cent of GDP as expenditure pressures challenge consolidation efforts, according to a Deutsche Bank Research report.
While the central government is on track to meet its fiscal deficit target of 4.3 per cent of GDP in FY27, the path forward presents steeper hurdles.
"The central government will most likely meet its FY27 fiscal deficit target of 4.3% of GDP; however, FY28 consolidation looks considerably more challenging.
Considering the various risks, we forecast the FY28 fiscal deficit to remain unchanged at 4.3% of GDP," the report stated.

Several cushions support the government's fiscal math in the current fiscal year, including a substantial Reserve Bank of India dividend of ₹2.9 lakh crore, an ₹1 lakh crore Economic Stabilisation Fund provision, potential capital expenditure compression, and higher-than-expected disinvestment receipts.
However, the subsequent fiscal year faces headwinds from persistently elevated oil prices, larger subsidy bills, a potentially lower central bank dividend, and the rollout of the 8th Pay Commission.
"Implementation of the 8th Pay Commission, which could add at least ₹3 lakh crore to expenditure.
Delaying the pay award to 2028 could provide near-term relief but would merely shift the burden forward through a larger accumulation of arrears," the report noted.
Despite fiscal and external challenges, the report maintains a steady view on economic expansion.
Real GDP growth is projected at 7.3 per cent year-on-year in FY27, 7.2 per cent in FY28, and 7.3 per cent in FY29.

Although a sub-normal monsoon, higher oil prices, and unfavourable base effects from last year's GST rate cuts are expected to moderate growth in the second half of FY27, the implementation of pay commission awards is anticipated to lift domestic demand next year.
"We remain broadly constructive on India's growth trajectory and general resilience of the economy despite the ongoing West Asia crisis and a sub-normal monsoon this year," the report added.

stories.headline: Supreme Court refuses to entertain plea to reduce minimum age for contesting elections
stories.title: Supreme Court refuses to entertain plea to reduce minimum age for contesting elections
stories.summary: When the bench observed that it was not an appropriate petition, the counsel said, ‘The respondent can just inform the petitioner what is the outcome of his representation’
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Saturday (November 28, 2026) refused to entertain a plea seeking to reduce the minimum age for contesting parliamentary and state legislature elections.

The counsel appearing for the petitioner told a bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh that while the voting age was reduced from 21 to 18, the minimum age to be a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 and 30 for the Rajya Sabha.
The counsel also referred to the minimum age to be a member of the state legislative assembly and state legislative council.
"In this petition, there is a small but very vital issue.
The voting age, by the (Constitution) sixty-first amendment, was reduced from 21 to 18," the counsel said.
When the bench observed that it was not an appropriate petition, the counsel said, "The respondent can just inform the petitioner what is the outcome of his representation."
"For that, you go to the high court under (Article) 226 for getting a direction for deciding your representation," the bench said.
The plea had made the Centre and the Election Commission as party respondents.
The counsel then said that he would like to withdraw his plea.
"Dismissed as withdrawn," the bench said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court orders Karthigai Deepam to be lit at ‘deepathoon’ on November 28; issues contempt notice
stories.title: Supreme Court orders Karthigai Deepam to be lit at ‘deepathoon’ on November 28; issues contempt notice
stories.summary: Bench directs Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, Madurai District Collector, temple authorities to be present for next hearing on Dec. 15; court sees ‘pre-meditated conspiracy' between State and temple trustees
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Rejecting the Tamil Nadu government’s claim that it stayed aloof from the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple management’s customary decisions, the Supreme Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) said non-compliance with its November 20 order to light the Karthigai Deepam at the deepathoon (stone pillar) atop the Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai amounted to “wilful disobedience” born of a “pre-meditated conspiracy” between the State and the temple trustees.

A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi ordered the Board of Trustees of the temple to be suspended before appointing two former High Court judges – former Chief Justice of Meghalaya High Court S. Vaidyanathan and former Madras High Court judge Justice V. Parthiban - to act as Receivers.
The court directed the Karthigai Deepam to be lit again on Saturday (November 28, 2026), this time on the stone pillar, as was originally ordered on November 20.
Central forces would provide security.
The Receivers have to ensure the ceremony is carried out in consultation with the temple stanikars.
However, the interim order would not grant any future equities in favour of any party.
The court made clear that its order was limited only to contempt petitions.
The main case on religious rights concerning the Thirupparankundram lamp-lighting row would be heard in the second week of January 2027.
The row stems from the claims of ownership over the hilltop.
The deepathoon is located near the Sikandar Badusha Dargah on top of the hill, while the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple is at the base of the hill.
The dargah side has claimed ownership of the hilltop, including the deepathoon site.
The court order comes two days after the ceremonial lamp was lit at the customary location – Deepa Mandapam – atop the hill and not as the Bench mandated.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Refuses Urgent Hearing on Plea Challenging Ramayana Film's Portrayal
stories.title: Supreme Court Refuses Urgent Hearing on Plea Challenging Ramayana Film's Portrayal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to entertain an urgent listing request in a petition challenging the portrayal of the Hindu epic Ramayana in a movie, observing that there was no reason for immediate judicial intervention as the film had already hit theatres.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observation after the petitioner's counsel sought an early hearing, alleging that the movie presented a distorted account of the epic.
Pointing out that the film was already running in cinemas, the CJI remarked that those interested in watching it had already had the opportunity to do so.
"The movie has already been released.
People who wanted to watch, they have already seen," the CJI said.
The petitioner's counsel argued that the film contained several factual distortions which could influence the younger generation.

The bench, however, was not persuaded by the submission and, responding to the objection, said filmmakers were entitled to present the epic from their own perspective and that anyone holding a contrary interpretation could express it through their own creative work.
"They have made a movie as they understand.
You make your movie as you want.
Don't waste time of the court.
If you have a counter-view about the epic, you make a movie on the counter-view," CJI Kant remarked.

stories.headline: 'Well-Researched Constructive Criticism of Judiciary Is Necessary & Welcome': Chief Justice M.S. Sonak Retires From Jharkhand High Court
stories.title: 'Well-Researched Constructive Criticism of Judiciary Is Necessary & Welcome': Chief Justice M.S. Sonak Retires From Jharkhand High Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: Chief Justice M.S. Sonak has retired from the Jharkhand High Court, reflecting on the importance of judicial humility, constructive criticism and the need for judges to look beyond legal pleadings to recognise the human suffering underlying every dispute.

In his farewell speech, Chief Justice Sonak emphasised that the judiciary as an institution is far greater than the individuals who serve it, and that judges must remain conscious of their constitutional responsibility to administer justice with compassion and equity.
“This entire experience of working with you all and for this great institution of ours has been very humbling.
The judiciary in general, and the Jharkhand High Court, which we were sworn in to serve, are far greater than individuals like me, who are but birds of passage.”

Reflecting on the history and legacy of the institution, Chief Justice Sonak acknowledged the contributions of the legal luminaries associated with the Jharkhand High Court and its predecessor, the Patna High Court.
“As I expressed, when demitting my office as a judge of the Bombay High Court, all told, I am not very comfortable with the general idea of praising judges for doing their judicial duties.
No one deserves praise for doing what he or she ought to do.”
“Therefore, well-researched and constructive criticism and course correction are welcome, and I should say, necessary.

But this should not be to run down the institution or its judges, but out of genuine concern that our institution fulfils the noble role assigned to it by our Constitution and that we all remain faithful to the oath we take before assuming office.”
“What always remains within our grasp, however, is to remain conscious that behind the mass of case papers thrust before us is a human face crying for justice.
Our endeavour must be to see whether we can, within the four corners of the law, do justice to that human.”

“Our endeavour must be to look beyond the cold print of a petition to the human face behind it, remembering that our constitutional duty is not merely to apply the law mechanically, but to administer justice with compassion and equity.”

stories.headline: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri again after Bengal sample fails
stories.title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri again after Bengal sample fails
stories.summary: Food regulator FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a packaged drinking water sample collected from its West Bengal plant failed laboratory testing, sources said. The sample tested positive for coliform bacteria, they added. This form of bacteria can enter water systems through sewage leaks or damaged pipes, among other pathways. This action marks the second instance of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioning prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd, a leading player in the packaged drinking water sector in the country. On Sunday, the FSSAI announced similar legal proceedings after a sample from one of Bisleri's plants in Goa also failed testing. The West Bengal sample was taken from a plant in Jalpaiguri's Telipara village. The presence of coliform bacteria was confirmed by both primary and referral laboratories.
